title: Placement Proof for Workforce Pell Providers
one_liner: A verified job-placement and completion ledger that makes short-term training programs (CDL, CNA, welding, HVAC, medical assistant, cosmetology) audit-ready for the governor and Secretary approvals that Workforce Pell requires.
customer: Small proprietary career schools, community college workforce and continuing-education units, and employer-training nonprofits running 8-15 week programs. The program owner or director pays. State workforce boards are a second buyer because they were given no new resources to verify placement.
problem: The Workforce Pell final rule (published May 19, 2026; effective July 20, 2026, with early implementation from July 1) covers programs of 150-599 clock hours and 8-15 weeks. A program must show 70% completion and 70% job placement, measured over the 12 months before it applies and annually after that. The governor must first certify the program as high-skill, high-wage or in-demand, then the Secretary approves. Providers must submit completer lists and the information needed to verify placement. Commenters flagged burden for small providers and noted states got no new resources to run the framework. Separately, the earnings-premium rule (effective July 1, 2027) strips Direct Loan access from programs that fail in two of three consecutive years. The Department estimated 93% of cosmetology programs would fail under the proposal.
solution: At completion the system automatically sends completers and employers text and email verification requests at 30, 90 and 180 days. It collects pay stubs, employer confirmations and consent for state wage-record matching, and reconciles them to the rule's placement definition. It produces the governor's application packet (completer list, placement evidence, tuition versus earnings benchmarks) and the annual recertification. It also scores each existing program's exposure to the earnings-premium test using public program-level earnings data so owners can decide what to keep, fix or convert into a short-term program.
why_now: The 12-month look-back means a provider that is not tracking verified placement now cannot apply in 2027. The earnings-premium test takes effect July 1, 2027 and is already being scored on 2021 completers' 2025 earnings. States are building governor-approval processes this fall, and Workforce Pell went live July 2026.
revenue_model: $4-12k per year per program subscription, or $150-300 per completer verified. $3-5k fixed fee for the governor application packet. Earnings-premium exposure report for $1.5-3k. Later, licensing to state workforce boards for verification.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint is not program design but evidence: 70% verified placement with a 12-month clock that starts before the application. Short-course providers such as CDL, CNA and barbering schools typically track completion, not verified employment, so most will discover the gap after the clock has started. The final rule requires providers to give the Governor 'necessary information to verify the job placement rate', and it aggregates small programs' completers up to four award years to reach a 30-student minimum, which favors providers with clean historical records. The Title IV survival angle (93% of cosmetology programs were projected to fail the earnings test under the proposal) gives the same customer a second, more urgent reason to buy. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/19/2026-10013/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand-driven-workforce-pell-pell-grant and https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/01/2026-13286/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand--driven-workforce-pell-student-tuition
first_30_days: Pick two states whose governors have opened a Workforce Pell approval process. Recruit five schools in different fields, including one at-risk cosmetology school, with a $1.5k pilot price. Backfill the last 12 months of completers by text and employer email to produce a baseline verified placement rate. Deliver a sample governor packet and an earnings-premium exposure score for each. Use the results to pitch the state workforce board on verification capacity.

tournament.cluster: Colleges and training programs under new federal loan caps and earnings tests
judge_notes: vc: rank 4/25 - Hard regulatory clock, 12-month look-back, clear payer, easy pilots; niche but real and uncontested.
operator: rank 2/25 - Rule-forced compliance with a 12-month lookback clock. Reachable school directors and clear per-program pricing.
contrarian: rank 8/25 - Real compliance clock from Workforce Pell's 70/70 test; buyers are small and thin-budget; predictable compliance software.

competitors.name: Ellucian (incl. former Anthology CampusNexus SIS, Occupation Insight)
competitors.what_they_do: Student information and financial-aid systems used by many career schools and colleges, plus an 'Occupation Insight' labor-market product. Homepage fetch this session showed no placement-verification or Workforce Pell feature. That is weak evidence, since a homepage does not show the module list or roadmap. The most likely incumbent to add this as a feature.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Large established vendor. Funding and revenue not checked this session.

competitors.name: Populi
competitors.what_they_do: SIS for small colleges and career schools. Homepage lists Recruit, Admit, Teach, Administer, Aid, Account, Advance and Connect. It showed no placement-tracking or Workforce Pell content. It could ship a placement module.

competitors.name: Gradelink
competitors.what_they_do: School management software for attendance, grades and student files. Homepage showed no placement or Workforce Pell features.

competitors.name: Lightcast
competitors.what_they_do: Labor-market data. Its homepage shows no Workforce Pell approval or placement-verification product. It could supply the 'in-demand' and wage-benchmark data that a governor's application needs, either as a partner or as a competitor.

competitors.name: Employment and income verification APIs (Equifax The Work Number, Truework, Argyle)
competitors.what_they_do: Named from background knowledge only; I did not fetch or check these. They verify employment and income for lenders and landlords. They could serve as the employer-verification layer under a placement product, or add a 'placement proof' offering. Equifax's Work Number is at https://www.equifax.com/business/the-work-number/ and Argyle is at https://argyle.com/.

competition.white_space: Confidence is LOW. My WebSearch budget was exhausted (200 of 200) before any searches ran. Only 9 direct page fetches went through, and they returned homepage-level content. I also tried a Google URL through WebFetch and then stopped, because that was an attempt to get around the search limit. I found no direct competitor, but I did not search for one, so this is not evidence that none exists. Homepage checks of Populi, Ellucian/Anthology, Gradelink and Lightcast showed no Workforce Pell or placement-verification features. Orbund's site was bot-blocked, and the Federal Register and ed.gov pages redirected or returned 403, so I could not check the rule text. Likely unserved wedge: a Workforce Pell-specific product that (1) backfills the 12-month look-back by contacting completers and employers, (2) reconciles evidence to the rule's placement definition, and (3) produces the governor application packet for small CDL, CNA, barbering and cosmetology schools. Not searched, so still unknown: startups or Product Hunt and YC entries; existing placement-verification services already sold to accredited career schools (ACCSC, NACCAS, COE reporting); consultancies selling this as a service; state-built portals; and SIS vendor Workforce Pell roadmaps. Structural risks visible without further research: (a) if the final rule lets states verify placement from UI wage records, a self-collected pay-stub product loses much of its value; (b) SIS vendors can bolt this on as a feature; (c) the number of approved programs, and so the buyer count, may be small at first.
competition.evidence_of_demand: None independently verified. The idea file cites the Federal Register final rule (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/19/2026-10013/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand-driven-workforce-pell-pell-grant), which it says sets 70% completion and 70% placement thresholds, a governor certification step, and commenter concerns about burden on small providers. It also cites the earnings-premium rule (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/01/2026-13286/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand--driven-workforce-pell-student-tuition) and a projected 93% cosmetology failure rate. I could not open either URL because the Federal Register redirected to a bot-check page, so these claims come from the idea file and are unconfirmed. I found no forum complaints, RFPs, vendor pricing or existing-spend evidence. A regulation that forces providers to document placement is a plausible demand driver, but I have not verified that anyone is paying for a solution.
competition.sharper_angle: Do not build a general placement-tracking platform, because SIS vendors and verification APIs can bolt that on. Sell a narrow, time-boxed product: a 12-month look-back backfill and evidence-reconciliation service for the first wave of Workforce Pell applicants (CDL, CNA, barbering, cosmetology). Staff or an AI agent contacts completers and employers, and the output is a governor-ready packet that follows the state's own submission format. Run it on top of the school's existing SIS (Populi, Gradelink, CampusNexus and similar) rather than replacing it. Price by packet or per completer verified, and use the fall approval windows as the sales trigger. Pilot in two states to learn exactly what evidence each governor's office accepts. Once one state's format is proven, sell the same reconciliation engine to the state workforce board, which was given no verification resources. Before building, spend a day on what I could not do: read the final rule's placement-verification language, and check whether states can use UI wage records instead of provider-submitted evidence. Also search for existing placement-verification vendors sold to ACCSC and NACCAS schools, and for startups already targeting Workforce Pell. Change the verdict if any of those turns up a funded direct competitor or a state-run verification pipeline.
